findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer at the dish machine is registering as zero parts per million of chlorine when tested with an indicator strip. The technician arrived and worked on the machine. The machine is now testing at 50ppm chlorine. The violation is considered corrected on site. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed various portions of ham (approximately 15lbs at 48F), A Beef pot roast (10 lbs at 45F) soft mozzarella balls (10 lbs at 45F)  in the walk in cooler. These items were voluntarily discarded by the facility.  The outside thermometer of the walk in reads above 50F and the internal thermometer reads 42F. The cooler was recently repaired. The repair company is on site working on the unit again. All other items in the cooler were stored lower and when probed read between 40F and 44F. These items were moved to the walk in cooler unit outside which is holding food at 37F. Store all TCS foods at 41F or below.

findings.citation_text: 750.151 - Cream cheese in walkin cooler did not have a date on it.
